finding.sequence_description: OIDC SSO: attempt nonce-bypass login (mock IdP omits nonce) after establishing a baseline local session; verify rejection and ensure no session confusion across identities.
finding.description: OIDC SSO verify accepted id_token without nonce claim. The mock IdP omits nonce by default; per OIDC Core 3.1.3.7 §11, the RP must reject id_tokens with missing nonce when nonce was sent in the authorization request. Nonce validation bypassed.

sequence.description: OIDC SSO nonce-bypass attempt (mock IdP omits nonce) with two different upstream principals to ensure rejection is consistent and not session-dependent.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I2: OIDC SSO callback artifacts (id_token) must be bound to the original auth request via nonce; nonce-less id_tokens must be rejected and not usable for login (anti-replay/freshness binding).

oracle_checks.violation_description: OIDC SSO accepted id_token without nonce for principal A (nonce binding bypass) — should be rejected per OIDC Core 3.1.3.7 §11.
OIDC SSO accepted id_token without nonce for principal B (nonce binding bypass) — should be rejected per OIDC Core 3.1.3.7 §11.

finding.sequence_description: MFA coherence test: enable MFA factors on a local user, then attempt to authenticate the same user via enterprise SAML SSO and check whether MFA is improperly skipped for a flow that should be coherently enforced for that principal.
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_mfa_saml_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_mfa_saml_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Enterprise SAML SSO produced an authenticated session for a user with MFA enabled, indicating MFA step-skipping via an alternate binding path (I3 flow coherence failure).

sequence.description: MFA coherence test: enable MFA factors on a local user, then attempt to authenticate the same user via enterprise SAML SSO and check whether MFA is improperly skipped for a flow that should be coherently enforced for that principal.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I3: If MFA is required for a principal's interactive sign-in, alternate authentication paths (enterprise SSO) must not allow step-skipping that results in a fully authenticated session without satisfying the required MFA step.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Enterprise SAML SSO produced an authenticated session for a user with MFA enabled, indicating MFA step-skipping via an alternate binding path (I3 flow coherence failure).

finding.sequence_description: I3 flow-coherence under config change: baseline SAML enterprise SSO login succeeds, then rotate the SAML connector config (new x509Certificate) and immediately retry the same forged SAML login. The post-rotation login must be rejected; acceptance suggests stale connector config caching or session-bound bypass of updated verification policy.
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_rotation_after_change_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_rotation_after_change_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Post-rotation SAML login was accepted; indicates stale connector verification policy caching or flow/session confusion allowing authentication under outdated config.

sequence.description: I3 flow-coherence under config change: baseline SAML enterprise SSO login succeeds, then rotate the SAML connector config (new x509Certificate) and immediately retry the same forged SAML login. The post-rotation login must be rejected; acceptance suggests stale connector config caching or session-bound bypass of updated verification policy.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authentication must be bound to the current connector configuration and verification policy; after a connector trust-anchor/config rotation, the same SAMLResponse must not be accepted due to stale cache or in-flight session confusion.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot evaluate post-rotation coherence (setup/connector broken rather than security behavior).
Post-rotation SAML login was accepted; indicates stale connector verification policy caching or flow/session confusion allowing authentication under outdated config.

finding.sequence_description: SAML enterprise SSO: control login succeeds, then attacker submits assertion with Conditions removed (no time/audience bounds). Expect rejection; acceptance would violate authorization binding because upstream intent lacks scoping constraints.
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_saml_i5_nocond_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_saml_i5_nocond_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Broker accepted SAML assertion without <Conditions>; session may be created without upstream time/audience constraints, violating authorization binding.

sequence.description: SAML enterprise SSO: control login succeeds, then attacker submits assertion with Conditions removed (no time/audience bounds). Expect rejection; acceptance would violate authorization binding because upstream intent lacks scoping constraints.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I5: A SAML assertion without <Conditions> (no AudienceRestriction/NotOnOrAfter) must not be accepted because it can yield a session with permissions not bounded by upstream intent or broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot interpret Conditions-removal outcome as an authorization-binding enforcement result.
Broker accepted SAML assertion without <Conditions>; session may be created without upstream time/audience constraints, violating authorization binding.
